# Native admissibility — four-child boundary

Documented before implementation or numerical execution. Analytical proof leads developed while framing this document are disclosed in SCOPE.md; this is not a claim that those leads were prospectively preregistered.

## Carrier and extension
Use the nonempty nested-support category of the accepted v16.52 interface. The new boundary is one ordered parent with FOUR children. Each child initially supplies the accepted interface on an arbitrary finite binary/ternary tree. A proof that joining returns the identical interface would support structural induction with arities 2,3,4; that consequence must be justified, not assumed.

For a finite nonempty ordered palette P, S_root=P. Every vertex has a nonempty support S_v subset P and every child support is contained in its parent. There are no weights, new labels outside P, extra native vertices, simultaneous moves, or physical interpretation.

At internal v, h_v is the minimum size of a label set intersecting every immediate child support. Candidate target q_v is an integer 1 through arity(v). A target profile and palette are EXACTLY ADMISSIBLE only if such a nested state with h_v=q_v exists. Membership in that integer range alone does not establish feasibility on a given palette. Infeasible palettes are excluded by a proved feasibility condition, never by filtering failed constructions.

A legal primitive adds or deletes ONE label incidence at ONE nonroot vertex, preserving nonemptiness, nesting and the fixed global root. Exactness is an endpoint condition; intermediate states remain natively admitted and need not have h=q.

The claimed path budget is sum over ALL internal vertices of |h_v-q_v| <=1 at every primitive. Leaf coordinates contribute zero. Root-support changes at an attached child are legal incidences, and their effect on the four-child parent must be checked. Child normalization can spend its unit only while the parent and all other subtrees are exact.

The independent scalar barriers B1, Binf and Bs keep their inherited meanings; no lexicographic surrogate replaces them. No fundamental time, dynamics, energy, metric, gravity, or dark-matter primitive is introduced.

## Feasibility language, without an assumed width formula
Let a_i be the proved minimum palette width for child i. The compact four-root feasibility question is whether four subsets A_i of a k-label palette, with |A_i|=a_i, have transversal number q. Its equivalence to native nested-state feasibility requires proof.

Use all 15 nonempty incidence regions C subset {1,2,3,4}, with integer multiplicity n_C>=0; root-only labels may occupy the empty region. Then |A_i|=sum over C containing i of n_C. The transversal number is the least number of available region types whose union is all four indices. Repeated labels of the same region type cannot improve a minimum cover. Region multiplicities determine capacity; region support determines the cover number. No ternary width recurrence is extrapolated.

## Decisive obligations
Return the SAME six interface clauses: exact palette feasibility; compact ordered canonical endpoint; finite fixed-root normalization with total excursion <=1; exact-interior role replacement; attached compact contraction; simultaneous label/order equivariance.

Separate:
1. failure of the old proof or a chosen construction;
2. a genuine impossibility of the specified interface;
3. a nonunit barrier, requiring admitted exact endpoints and a lower bound excluding EVERY unit path.

A finite search failure, timeout, or unsuccessful normalization does not establish 2 or 3.

# What another index can learn from native move admissibility

Date: 2026-10-14 America/Phoenix / 2026-10-15 UTC.
Immutable source parent: `c63bc3ea9b92241fb96d52fe5e47dde16fd97c6b`.

**Conditional analytical classification; physical enforcement and access remain open.** The preceding assessment ruled out reading the first-response bit from other indices' unchanged membership views. This note tests a different candidate: whether the internal incidence change alters the receiver's available native moves and thereby supplies an indirect response.

The answer separates two facts. In the bare fixed-carrier nested-support category, all external information affecting a coalition's atomic moves is whether another index covers each global leaf. Changes confined to other indices' internal incidences leave the coalition's entire command interface unchanged. Global-leaf coverage differences can change that interface, but a physical mechanism enforcing the relation and delivering a readable outcome remains an additional obligation.

These are elementary deductions from the inherited move definition. They are not a new physical interaction, a mathematical priority claim, or an obstruction to all richer event laws.

## 1. Exact category and proposed interface

Fix a finite rooted tree T with root o and a fixed finite palette P. Each support S_v is nonempty, S_o=P, and child supports are contained in parent supports. Write

    Y_i = {v in T : i in S_v}.

The inherited atomic primitive adds or deletes one index incidence at one nonroot vertex while preserving those conditions. T and P stay fixed. This is the bare native admissibility of the cited v16.53 definition. Its separately stated hitting-profile path budget is NOT part of this transition relation. Neither C3 floors, protected supports, a scheduler, event rates, guaranteed acceptance, nor a physical legality oracle is inferred from the definition.

Fix a nonempty proper coalition C of receiver indices. The mathematical interface under test consists of its complete own views (Y_i) for i in C, the common T,P and references, and the admissibility of named atomic commands on those indices. To give the candidate its strongest version, one may hypothetically allow exact legality queries, execution of any admitted command, and observation of the resulting own views. This is a test interface, not already-earned native access. A rejected command leaves the state unchanged in that hypothetical query protocol; rejection flags are not supplied by the native category itself.

Only indices in C act during a receiver experiment. Indices outside C are held fixed in each compared state. Exogenous events, changing carriers, rates, timing, notifications and extra guards are separate interfaces.

Let L_*(T) be the nonroot global leaves of T, and define the external coverage set

    E_C(F) = {l in L_*(T) : some j outside C belongs to S_l(F)}.

This records existence of outside coverage, not the identities or number of outside owners. It is a sufficient mathematical description of external influence on this relation; the receiver is not assumed to start knowing E_C.

## 2. Exact one-command conditions

For i in C and v != o, addition +i(v) is admitted exactly when

    v not in Y_i,                 parent(v) in Y_i.

Nonemptiness is preserved by an addition. Nesting at the parent requires the second condition. Since i was absent from v, nesting in the initial valid state already excludes i from all children of v. Hence no other index membership is consulted.

Deletion -i(v) is admitted exactly when v belongs to Y_i, v is a tip of Y_i, and one of the following holds:

- v is internal in T; or
- v is a global leaf and either another coalition index contains v or v belongs to E_C(F).

The tip condition means no immediate child of v belongs to Y_i; prefix closure makes this equivalent to absence of all strict own-view descendants. It is precisely the nesting condition after deletion.

For the internal-vertex case, choose any child w of v. Its support is nonempty. Since i is absent from every child, some j != i belongs to S_w, and nesting gives j in S_v. Thus another index necessarily retains v; nonemptiness at v is automatic. For a global leaf there is no such descendant witness, and the displayed coverage condition is exactly S_v minus {i} being nonempty. This proves necessity and sufficiency in every case.

The argument is about valid mathematical states, not an event obtaining the terminal fact, the carrier, or the outside-coverage fact. In particular, a fact forced in a full-state proof need not be available as an executable local certificate.

## 3. Exact receiver interface through finite command histories

Suppose F and G have the same T,P, the same own views for every i in C, and the same E_C. Then:

1. Every named coalition command is admitted in F exactly when it is admitted in G.
2. Performing the same admitted command changes the same own incidence and leaves the outside indices fixed. The two successors again have identical coalition views and E_C.
3. An exact legality query gives the same answer in both, and a rejected query changes neither state.

The first statement follows directly from section 2; the second and third preserve its premises. Induction therefore gives identical admissibility answers and own-view observations along every finite adaptive coalition-command experiment using only this interface. Equivalently, the two command transition systems are related by an observation-preserving labelled bisimulation: matching commands remain possible and lead to matching interface states.

For a common processing/randomization rule driven only by these answers, own views, and source-independent reference/local-memory inputs, the transcript laws also coincide. This does NOT mean arbitrary physical processes with the same unweighted move graph have the same probabilities. A separately justified hidden-state-dependent rate or resolution law could differ; the bare relation supplies no such law. Source-dependent timing, availability or stopping signals must not be smuggled into an allegedly identical transcript.

The external coverage set is also necessary for equivalence of the FULL command interface when initial own views agree. Suppose a nonroot global leaf l is externally covered in F but not G. Validity of G requires at least one coalition owner at l; by identical own views the same owners occur in F. Choose one such owner i. Delete each other coalition owner's incidence at l, leaving i in place. These are global-leaf deletions admitted in both states, because i continues covering l. They do not change E_C. Now -i(l) is admitted in F and forbidden in G. Thus a finite successful-command language differs, and an exact final legality query would distinguish the states.

This necessity claim assumes the full interface, including the specified admitted preparatory commands. A smaller physically available command family may reveal less. It does not promise completion, a readable rejection, or execution of every legal request.

Consequently, with fixed T,P and own-view observations, the pair

    ((Y_i) for i in C, E_C)

is an exact quotient of the bare coalition-command interface. External internal incidences carry no further information through this particular relation. This is stronger than a static unchanged-view statement because receiver actions, including additions and actual safe global-leaf deletions, are allowed throughout the comparison.

## 4. Application to the existing first-response bit

Use the inherited first-response source pair and its permitted a-view contractions. For each source separately, compare its state immediately before a proper output with its state immediately after that output.

Every other index's view is unchanged. Every global-leaf incidence of a is unchanged as well: the mandatory hull retains each such incidence and outputs only contract. The changes occur solely at internal vertices of T. Therefore, for ANY fixed C not containing a, the two states have the same coalition views and the same E_C.

Sections 2-3 apply. No finite experiment confined to the coalition's own views and the bare carrier-preserving atomic-command interface can tell whether that internal a-view change occurred. This remains true even when the candidate receiver is hypothetically granted all actual safe native commands, rather than being restricted to the earlier universal independent-view contraction class.

In source one, every proper output changes the inherited bit

    R = 1[h_p > 1] = 1[U is not a subset of Z_a]

from zero to one. The receiver-command interface above is nevertheless unchanged across that actual mathematical transition. Thus carrier-preservation admissibility cannot by itself turn this internal R change into a newly accessible receiver response. A fresh receipt or direct a-membership read would be an additional channel.

This is a BEFORE/AFTER claim within each source. It is NOT a claim that the two source preparations have identical command interfaces. They differ in global-leaf a-incidences before any action. For example choose C={b_2}, which exists for m>=2. At r_2 the supports are {a,b_2} in source zero and {b_2} in source one. The command -b_2(r_2) is already admitted in source zero and forbidden in source one. Granting an exact readable legality oracle would therefore reveal a source distinction BEFORE the first-response event. Counting that pre-existing interface difference as a record produced by the internal event would misidentify the acquisition step.

The original conditional first-response theorem and its positive restricted a-view decoder remain intact. The present result stops the specific attempt to obtain an additional receiver connection from bare carrier-safety feedback.

## 5. Controls and ways outside the result

**A genuine leaf change can alter another index's menu.** On the binary tree T={o,l,r} and P={a,b}, start with S_l=S_r={a,b}. The admitted action -a(l) leaves S_l={b} and S_r unchanged. For receiver C={b}, -b(l) was admitted before and is forbidden afterward. Here E_C really changes. Both states remain valid and the source action is proper. The restriction to unchanged external leaf coverage is therefore essential; the theorem does not prohibit cross-index constraint dependence at global leaves.

**The inherited unit-band guard can distinguish the same bare interfaces.** In source one of the inherited family with m=2, compare the state before -a(u_1) with the state after it. Their total deficits from the same all-one reference q are respectively zero and one; both satisfy D_q<=1. Use C={b_1,c}. In both states the leaf supports at r_1,w_1 are {b_1,c}. First execute -b_1(r_1). The two child supports become {c} and {b_1,c}, so h_(u_1) remains one; both states still satisfy the unit band. Next request -c(w_1). The children would become {c} and {b_1}, making h_(u_1)=2. Both commands are bare-native admitted in both comparisons. But the final total deficit would be one before the a-event and two after it. An exact D_q<=1 transition guard therefore permits the second command in the former case and rejects it in the latter. This is a conditional two-command discriminator using the inherited band, with BOTH starting states in the band. It neither implements that global guard nor supplies readable rejection or commit-every-legal-request semantics. It identifies precisely why the bare-interface classification must not be promoted to a full C3-guarded impossibility theorem.

**Direct access and other events remain eligible.** A receiver that reads changed a-membership, an internal component of the a-view, an authentic event receipt, a derived joint operation, a changed-carrier process or a justified probability law can have more information. Their availability must be established on their own terms. The theorem does not require every receiver to be a separate palette index or every physical process to fit this transition relation.

**Admissibility is not actuation.** The leaf control and the completeness proof provide conditional admitted-command distinctions. They do not derive a mechanism that resolves requests, exposes rejection, schedules events or retains a result. The earlier nested-record screen already preserved this distinction. No repetition of an all-NOOP argument is needed here.

## 6. Scientific decision

Disposition: **BARE_MOVE_INTERFACE_CLASSIFIED_BY_EXTERNAL_LEAF_COVERAGE; INTERNAL_FIRST_RESPONSE_NOT_TRANSMITTED_BY_THIS_INTERFACE; NATIVE_ACCESS_OPEN.**

The advance is a precise location of possible cross-index dependence in the inherited bare atomic relation. External global-leaf coverage can affect a receiver's command possibilities. External internal-incidence changes cannot, even after finite receiver-command sequences, when the other stated inputs are held fixed. The first-response construction changes the internal profile while remaining in one such receiver-interface class.

This gives the next candidate a concrete test. To use carrier-safety interaction, it must justify an event that changes the relevant external leaf coverage and a readable command consequence. To use the already-proved internal response, it must justify another channel, such as actual access to a-membership or a derived guarded/joint transition law. Neither a full-state validator nor a desired hitting-profile readout supplies that mechanism. The positive-extension safety contract preserves every global-leaf incidence, so its contractions alone cannot change E_C for an untouched receiver coalition.

The result is conditional mathematical progress and a bounded receiver-candidate rejection. It does not establish a new physical force, native event, sensor, geometry, energy, clock, dark-matter variable or gravity explanation. The frontier milestone remains NOT ACHIEVED; Path A stays active and Path B closed. Time remains pruning / ordered recoverability update. Broad C3/C4-C6 and physical origin remain open.

No scientific code, enumeration, simulation or numerical campaign was run. The proof and analytical controls were developed before any possible numerical preregistration. Text/hash/source checks are provenance work and add no historical scientific test count. No main merge or numbered-stage CLOSED/CERTIFIED status is claimed. Independent whole-argument review and separate source/publication auditing are recorded alongside this note.

The ten-source packet binds the native move definition, positive-extension result, first-response theorem, own-view assessment, native dependency ledger, earlier nested-record screen, milestone, physical-frontier decision, AGENTS and parent continuation. These sources establish the declared premises and prior boundaries. No archive-wide originality or absence claim is made.

# Source withdrawal makes the first proper receiver pruning informative

Date: 2026-10-17 America/Phoenix. Author: proteinfolding-gpt.
Immutable source baseline: 89dab026b5312408cde3a98fd2f9ea416d3027ad.
Status: analytical construction frozen for independent review; native event/access NOT_DERIVED.

## 1. Positive construction and the premise removed

The accepted own_view_completion_review construction needs exact terminal root hitting number h_o=2. This construction replaces that target-conditioned completion by a simpler, explicit event class: after the same source withdrawal in both preparations, only the same receiver r prunes its own incidences while external indices remain fixed.

For the preparations below, EVERY proper receiver-pruning output already distinguishes the source in r's COMPLETE own view. The first native atomic r-deletion suffices, wherever it occurs. No hitting-profile constraint, maximal-pruning condition, target return, receiver completion flag or exact endpoint is needed. Both full initial own views are identical; even their entire bare r-command interfaces are initially equivalent.

This is a new synthesis of inherited native legality and the external-leaf-coverage classification, not a new physical law or mathematical priority claim. The source phase and occurrence of a proper receiver-pruning event are still conditional. Restricting the responding actor to r, fixing the other views, and using pruning rather than arbitrary subsequent additions are declared protocol premises, not consequences of bare legality. Own-view availability remains open. No event resolver or reader is coded.

## 2. Native carrier and preparations

Use the same finite rooted shape as the accepted construction:

    T = {o,w} disjoint-union U disjoint-union V.                (1)

The root o has exactly three children u,v,w. U=desc[u] and V=desc[v] are arbitrary finite nonempty rooted cones; w is a leaf. The fixed palette is P={a,b,r}, S_o=P and S_w={r}. Nonempty supports nest from children to parents. The native primitive changes one label incidence at one nonroot vertex, retaining these conditions.

Prepare:

| Region | s=0 | s=1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| every vertex in U | {a,r} | {a,b,r} |
| every vertex in V | {a,b,r} | {a,r} |
| w | {r} | {r} |
| o | {a,b,r} | {a,b,r} |

Write A_0=U, B_0=V and A_1=V, B_1=U. A_s is the branch without b; B_s is the branch with b. These are proof labels, not instructions supplied to the receiver.

In both preparations:

    Y_r = {z : r belongs to S_z} = T.                         (2)

This deliberately changes the earlier construction's initial receiver view from {o,w} to T. No acquisition is credited to adding r along a source-dependent path; r is already everywhere and identically so in both cases. The only preparation difference is b's view. The full initial hitting profile is all ones in both cases, although the theorem imposes no target profile.

## 3. Preparation and stronger initial blindness

A common seed has S_z={a,b,r} everywhere in U union V, with the same root and w. Delete b throughout U in child-before-parent order to obtain s=0, or throughout V to obtain s=1. These native paths preserve nesting, nonemptiness, the complete receiver view T, the common a-view and the all-one hitting profile. This proves relative common-seed reachability, not physical generation of that seed or certified physical source preparation.

The receiver_move_interface theorem classifies the bare command interface for C={r} by (Y_r,E_r), with E_r the externally covered nonroot global leaves. Initially,

    E_r = L(U) union L(V)                                     (3)

in BOTH preparations, because a covers all of those leaves and w is exclusively r. Thus not only Y_r but the entire inherited bare r-command interface agrees: the same finite adaptive r-command experiment has matching legality answers and own-view transcripts under that hypothetical interface, while the external indices are fixed.

This uses the inherited classification rather than claiming a new theorem about operational equivalence. It concerns the named bare command relation, not unprovided hidden-dependent rates, timing, joint-label experiments or other observations. The concrete protocol starts from the unmodified preparations (2); arbitrary earlier r-experiments are not inserted into its starting state.

## 4. Same source operation, with no receiver repair

Let D=U union V. In both preparations request exactly the same list of a-deletions: one at every vertex in D, in a common child-before-parent ordering. During this source phase r and b are fixed. Every deletion is legal in both cases because r remains at every vertex and the a-deletion order preserves nesting. There is no initially disabled deletion requiring a hidden source-dependent r-addition.

After all these a-deletions have occurred:

    S_z={r}       for z in A_s,
    S_z={b,r}     for z in B_s,
    S_w={r},      S_o=P,
    Y_r=T.                                                    (4)

The source phase itself does NOT change r's view. It changes the external leaf coverage from (3) to E_r=L(B_s). The response proved next comes from native cross-index coverage constraints after that withdrawal. No receiver is assumed to read E_r or the b-view.

Source withdrawal here is a supplied finite ordered operation list on existing primitives. Its enactment and the physical ordering that places a receiver response after it are not derived. There is no inference from submitting a command to its commitment and no source-completion notification is granted to r.

## 5. Every proper receiver-pruning output separates

After (4), keep a and b fixed, keep the root and carrier fixed, and permit only native r-deletions at nonroot vertices. All such deletions use the inherited bare grammar; there is no profile budget, target guard or extra deletion-site restriction. An identity or prematurely stopped history remains possible.

**Theorem 1.** The reachable receiver views are exactly the prefix-closed Z satisfying

    {o,w} union A_s  subseteq Z subseteq T.                    (5)

Consequently every proper output Z != T has a nonempty missing set

    empty != M=T minus Z subseteq B_s.                        (6)

For the same source-independent role r, the two sets of proper output views are disjoint.

Proof. Every vertex of A_s and w has r as its sole remaining label by (4). Nonemptiness forbids removing r there. Root membership is fixed and native nesting makes Z prefix closed. This proves (5) for every reachable state, and (6) for any proper state.

Conversely, let Z be prefix closed and satisfy (5). Delete r at every vertex of T minus Z, in deepest-first order. These vertices all lie in B_s and retain b. Nonemptiness therefore holds. Prefix closure of Z and deepest-first deletion ensure that no retained r-child lies below an r-incidence being deleted; the parent relation is preserved. Every deletion is a legal native atomic move. This realizes Z and proves exact reachability. Since U and V are disjoint, no nonempty missing set can be contained in both B_0=V and B_1=U. QED.

**Corollary 1 (first primitive).** Immediately after (4), the exact set of admitted r-deletions is

    {-r(l) : l is a global leaf in B_s}.                       (7)

Every cone has at least one such leaf. All internal vertices still have r-children, so deleting r there would violate nesting. Leaves in A_s and w are solely covered by r, so deleting r there would violate nonemptiness. Leaves in B_s retain b and admit deletion. This proves (7), including existence of at least one proper option in each source case.

Thus no selected location or completed relaxation is needed: ANY actual first r-pruning event in this declared phase produces a source-specific own view. The proof establishes what a proper event must do, not that an event occurs or has positive probability.

**Corollary 2 (persistent partial record).** Along subsequent r-pruning with the external views fixed, M grows by inclusion and remains in B_s. Once nonempty it remains nonempty, so the same source answer stays valid at every later prefix. No end-of-pruning acknowledgment is needed for this post-source-phase decoder. This is retention under the declared pruning grammar, not retention under arbitrary native edits or carrier changes.

The identity view Z=T is common to both cases and decodes as UNKNOWN. Zero response must not be assigned a source value.

## 6. Structural readout in the six-vertex witness

Choose U={u,x,y}, where x,y are children of u, and V={v}. Thus T={o,u,x,y,v,w}. The same rooted structure and receiver role are reference data in both preparations.

The initial and post-source receiver view is T in both cases. The first proper responses are:

| Source | All admitted first r-deletions | Full resulting view |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | -r(v) | T minus {v} |
| 1 | -r(x), -r(y) | T minus {x}, or T minus {y} |

All these first output views have cardinality FIVE. The previous endpoint size decoder (5 versus 3) must NOT be reused here.

Instead define a partial decoder on the receiver's current own view and the same known T:

    d(T) = UNKNOWN;
    d(Z) = 1 if a depth-two vertex of T is missing from Z;
    d(Z) = 0 if v is missing and no depth-two vertex is missing. (8)

Only reachable outputs in (5) are claimed. In source 0, the only possible missing vertex is v. In source 1, any nonempty missing set contains x or y: removal of u also requires removing both descendants. Therefore (8) is sound at EVERY nonidentity receiver-pruning prefix after source withdrawal.

Depth means finite ancestor-chain length in the existing rooted tree, not a physical metric or fundamental time. The unique branching child u, its depth-two leaves and the receiver role transport under simultaneous tree/palette relabeling. The tests in (8) therefore do not depend on literal vertex names or an added cross-carrier dictionary. No source-dependent reference or b-view is read.

If own-view access is physically available, (8) is sufficient. Neither the existence of this function nor naming Z as an owned view derives that availability.

## 7. Optional terminal consequence, not a premise

A receiver-pruning state is unextendible exactly when

    Z = {o,w} union A_s.                                      (9)

If a vertex in B_s remains in Z, choose a deepest remaining one. It is an r-tip with b coverage and so admits deletion. Conversely, at (9) every nonroot retained r-incidence is required by exclusive coverage or nesting. This proves the unique native pruning normal form. Every sequence of proper r-deletions has length at most |B_s|; actual continuation to a sink is not asserted.

At (9), supports are {r} throughout A_s and {b} throughout B_s; w={r}. Hence h_o=2 and every other internal hitting number is one. The old exact-target endpoint is a CONSEQUENCE of unextendibility for this revised preparation and pruning class, rather than an imposed profile guard. The first-response result in sections 5-6 does not require unextendibility.

This is an elementary application of native atomic descent, related to pruning_saturation. The contribution here is the source-to-same-owner response with complete initial interface blindness and a first-event decoder, not the finite termination argument itself.

## 8. Controls and limits on the protocol

**Before source withdrawal, the same deletion can occur in both cases.** In the six-vertex fixture, -r(v) is legal initially in both because a covers v. It would misleadingly produce the source-0 record even in source 1. Thus the post-source phase is load-bearing. The theorem gives no all-phase decoder, source-completion flag, timing signal or way for r to verify that the source phase has finished.

**The first source phase writes no own-view record.** Y_r remains T across every a-deletion. Its changed native response possibilities are a dependence available to the joint relation, not an already observed bit. A proper r-response is needed to turn it into a differing own view.

**Post-response additions can erase the record.** In either case, reverse a single admitted r-deletion by the corresponding legal r-addition; the receiver view returns to T. Thus persistence is specific to receiver pruning. The first-step source classification is stronger than the persistence claim in one respect: from Y_r=T, a proper first receiver-only atomic edit cannot be an addition because no r-incidence is absent. Its direction is forced to be a deletion by saturation of the INITIAL r-view. This does not prevent later additions, and does not select the actor r or force any event.

**Other labels acting can give no receiver response.** After (4), b may legally be deleted at a leaf of B_s while r remains there. That is a proper native event with Y_r unchanged. Consequently "every proper event" would be false without the explicitly receiver-owned response class.

**Source stability matters.** Restoring a or changing b alters exclusive coverage and can invalidate the decoder. Fixing the external views during the r-response is an inherited receiver-experiment contract, not a new conservation law.

**No hidden legality oracle.** Formula (7) is proved from the joint native state; the receiver need not be given it as input. There is no implementation that queries hidden supports, resolves a request, emits a rejection flag or records a chosen command. Any such implementation would supply the still-open action/access connection.

## 9. What is earned, what remains, and how to stay on target

| Obligation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Common preparation | Legal paths from a common seed; physical generation remains open |
| Initial receiver blindness | Same COMPLETE view and same bare receiver-command interface |
| Common source withdrawal | Identical legal a-command list in both cases, with no receiver precursor |
| New dependence | Withdrawal changes external leaf coverage while Y_r stays equal |
| Response consequence | Every proper first receiver-only atomic event is a deletion and yields a source-specific full own view |
| Completion/profile requirement | Removed from first-response claim |
| Retention | Source answer persists through further r-pruning with external views fixed |
| Source enactment, response occurrence, actor/phase selection | NOT DERIVED |
| Physical own-view/reference access | NOT DERIVED |
| New mechanism in code | None |

Compared with first_event_separation, the receiver's entire initial own view is blind, not merely a restricted projection of an already source-distinguishing view. Compared with own_view_completion_review, the post-source response uses bare native legality and needs neither exact-target return nor receiver completion. The preparation has changed, and the all-add/delete completion theorem is not being claimed without its target.

The source of cross-index dependence is precisely the inherited receiver_move_interface classification: external GLOBAL LEAF coverage affects r's legal deletion relation. This construction uses that existing fact positively; it does not count it again as a discovery. The mathematical improvement is a composition in which the interface starts blind, the same source operation exposes that dependence, and every proper first r-event places the answer into the same complete own view.

This narrows the native target to an enacted source withdrawal followed by a proper r-event and physically available own-view output. No terminal-profile sensor or maximal-pruning scheduler is required. It is still a conditional native-grammar construction, NOT a derivation of physical occurrence or access. The next work must earn one of those interfaces from sources rather than repeat this witness with larger trees.

## 10. Review contract and scientific scope

All proofs and controls were developed analytically before this freeze; they are already-known findings, not prospective numerical predictions. Independent Gemini review must reconstruct them, assess whether the new composition removes a genuine premise, and challenge any claim of physical closure. Nine exact source files are bound by source_packet.json and source_lock.json.

No simulator, enumerator, numerical campaign or archived scientific module is executed. Existing synthetic review/provenance tests check the pipeline only. No main merge, numbered-stage CLOSED/CERTIFIED status, broad C3 closure, empirical breakthrough, new particle, geometry, fundamental clock or physical force is claimed.
